leaks.how_it_shows: You co-produce easily, so you say yes to a partner before the split is written down. The Companion weight at eight means working alongside someone is natural, and the Eating God weight means you ship the first draft fast — often before the terms are settled. You then find yourself doing the work while the split is still verbal, and the Seven Killings filter starts editing your output to avoid conflict. The leak is not the partnership; it is the unwritten split.
leaks.rule: If you are about to start co-producing with someone, then write the split and the deliverable in one page before the first draft ships; if the other person will not sign the one page, then do not ship the first draft.

leaks.how_it_shows: You give the honest opinion before someone asks, and you are the one who calls the colleague who will actually do something. That makes you the default fixer in your circle. The Companion weight at eight means you are comfortable being the first to move if someone is moving with you, so you say yes to the request before you check your own shipping block. The leak shows up as a week where you produced for everyone else and shipped nothing of your own.
leaks.rule: If a request arrives that is not on your shipping block for the week, then reply with a specific later date and do not start it before that date; if the request cannot wait, then name the one piece of your own output that will slip and decide which one to drop.

leaks.how_it_shows: You draft the email before the requirements are finalized and build the rough prototype before the budget is approved. leaks.rule: If a commitment costs more than a day of your output, then wait one full shipping cycle before you commit; if the commitment still looks right after you have shipped one piece of your own work, then commit.
